card.name: Early words in news commentary clauses
card.fires_on: Short function or filler words that open a clause in news or science prose, such as 'our' after 'In', 'exciting', 'Hopefully', 'really', or an opening bracket before a name. The next word is usually a subject or noun.

modes.label: Clause openers
modes.description: Pronouns, determiners or adverbs starting a clause in quoted or reported speech.
modes.example: In<< our>> continent, unfortunately, that is not always

modes.label: Evaluative words
modes.description: Adjectives or adverbs giving an opinion about findings or events.
modes.example: The findings are<< exciting>> because they support a well-documented method

modes.label: Bracket before name
modes.description: An opening square bracket inserted before a person's name in a quote.

card.plain: It fires on small words that start a clause in news stories, just before the main subject or point comes.
